plan.title: Computer use on Windows (WSL2): drive the Windows desktop with Orca's PowerShell helper
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: Already one of three sibling issues (5461 seam, 5462 Windows, 5463 macOS). The projected surface is about 29 files across many path prefixes (vendored script, port-lint scripts, CI workflow, skill, mdx page, changelog, lib, cli, frontend). Most are small edits or tests. Splitting further would ship a Windows provider without its key rules, docs or CI proof.

narratives.Problem: pan computer and Settings → Computer Use only drive Linux desktops. Overdeck on Windows runs inside WSL2, where the Linux helper would drive WSLg windows instead of the Windows desktop, so PAN-5461 refuses WSL until a Windows provider exists.
narratives.Proposal: Vendor Orca's runtime.ps1 (MIT, c6b9ac9549b, UI Automation, nothing to install), copy it to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Overdeck\computer-use\ and run it one-shot through WSL interop with powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass. Add a wsl provider on PAN-5461's seam (bridge, readiness probes, Windows blocked-key table), surface it in doctor, capabilities and Settings, document it and prove it on a windows-2022 runner. Only vendoring and the native CI job run before PAN-5461 merges; every other item task_blocks until then.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Must not create, redefine or stub any part of the PAN-5461 seam: platform.ts types/detectPlatform/providerFor (beyond one `case 'wsl'` line), the platform parameter of assertKeyComboAllowed, the doctor/readiness refactor, or ComputerUseSection.tsx
- Native Windows Overdeck (no WSL) and WSL1
- Orca's persistent -Serve mode or any latency work beyond measuring it
- Edits to the body of the vendored runtime.ps1, or fixes for its known limits (main window only, mixed DPI, elevated apps)
- New ComputerUseErrorCode values for Windows message prefixes
- New route-scopes.ts rows or new dashboard routes
- Making the computer-use-windows workflow a required check

autoDecisions.summary: Record upstream commit c6b9ac9549b for runtime.ps1
autoDecisions.rationale: Every other Orca record uses it, and runtime.ps1 at c6b9ac9549b is byte-identical to Orca HEAD (verified), so the port lint and diff tooling stay uniform.

autoDecisions.summary: Bridge throws helper_error on ok:false instead of returning the response
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches helper.ts on Linux; run.ts and commands assume a returned response succeeded. The original PRD wording contradicted that contract.
Same as the Linux helper; helper.ts's ExecFileFn requires killSignal, and a 4K screenshot in base64 can exceed 20 MiB.

autoDecisions.summary: Go straight to -ExecutionPolicy Bypass (no RemoteSigned retry like Orca)
autoDecisions.rationale: Overdeck writes the script locally itself; a retry would double a one-shot call's cost. Group Policy blocks get a clear message.

autoDecisions.summary: Cache the resolved helper dir on disk
autoDecisions.rationale: Each pan computer command is a new process; resolving %LOCALAPPDATA% costs an extra powershell.exe start (~0.5 s) per command otherwise.

autoDecisions.summary: CI on windows-2022 with Vampire/setup-wsl@v7 and a packed tarball
autoDecisions.rationale: windows-smoke.yml (PAN-4331) proved WSL2 works there; installing a tarball avoids building from a CRLF /mnt checkout and proves packaging.
WSL1 has no WSLInterop binfmt entry; Overdeck documents WSL2 as the Windows path.

autoDecisions.summary: Window-targeting prefixes stay inside helper_error messages
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids widening the error-code union for one platform; the skill teaches agents to read the prefix.

autoDecisions.summary: The computer-use-windows workflow also triggers on push (paths-filtered)
autoDecisions.rationale: The pipeline opens the PR only at pan done, so a pull_request-only trigger would make the CI ACs circular; windows-smoke.yml uses the same push trigger.

autoDecisions.summary: Capabilities label comes from windowsVersion(), not the handshake or readiness()
autoDecisions.rationale: The handshake has no OS build, and readiness() would run a second handshake; one PowerShell version probe is cheap and gives a single defined source.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the WSL_INTEROP guard (D-17) and record a CI checkpoint for it
autoDecisions.rationale: The guard only acts when the variable is missing, so it can't break a working env; the CI checkpoint records the evidence and a failure turns into a follow-up issue.

items.title: Vendor Orca's runtime.ps1 with its upstream port record

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2, D-9, D-13, D-14. Independent of PAN-5461; do it first. Create native/computer-use-windows/runtime.ps1 from `git -C ~/Projects/orca show c6b9ac9549b:native/computer-use-windows/runtime.ps1` (never the Orca working tree), prepending exactly two ASCII lines: `# Ported from Orca (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Lovecast Inc.)` and `# upstream: native/computer-use-windows/runtime.ps1 @ c6b9ac9549b`. No BOM, LF endings, body untouched. Append the record {local,upstream:'orca',path,commit:'c6b9ac9549b'} to scripts/upstream-ports.json. In scripts/upstream-port-diff.sh change `if [[ "$local_path" == *.py ]]` to also match *.ps1 and update the comment there and the top-of-file comment (line ~14). Write native/computer-use-windows/README.md modeled on native/computer-use-linux/README.md: what the script is (Orca's Windows UI Automation bridge, MIT, commit c6b9ac9549b), that Overdeck copies it to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Overdeck\computer-use\ and runs it from WSL2 with `powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File runtime.ps1 <op.json>` (one process per operation, one JSON line out), and how to re-vendor (git show at a new commit, bump the commit in both header and record, run `bash scripts/upstream-port-diff.sh orca` first).

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7 step 1 and step 3. Independent of PAN-5461 (only needs the vendored script). Create .github/workflows/computer-use-windows.yml: name computer-use-windows; on workflow_dispatch, and on push and pull_request with paths native/computer-use-windows/**, src/lib/computer-use/**, .github/workflows/computer-use-windows.yml; permissions contents: read; env OVERDECK_TELEMETRY: '0'. Job `native` on windows-2022, timeout 15 min: checkout; a pwsh step starts notepad.exe and sleeps 3 s; for each op (handshake, list_apps, {"tool":"get_app_state","app":"notepad"}) write the JSON to $env:RUNNER_TEMP, run `powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File native/computer-use-windows/runtime.ps1 <op>`, measure wall-clock with Measure-Command, append op name + seconds + ok to $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. Handshake must be ok:true with capabilities.platform == 'win32' (fail the job otherwise). The get_app_state check (ok:true, non-empty snapshot.treeLines, non-null snapshot.screenshotPngBase64) is soft: on failure print the response and write 'Notepad tree/screenshot not available on the hosted desktop' to the summary without failing. Mirror the conventions of .github/workflows/windows-smoke.yml. Push the branch over SSH (`git push git@github.com:eltmon/overdeck.git feature/pan-5462`) because the gh token lacks the workflow scope.

Windows bridge: run runtime.ps1 through WSL interop (wsl-bridge.ts)

metadata.acJustification: Six ACs: the bridge is the one foundation item and each AC pins a distinct failure-mapping or environment rule the provider and CI depend on.

narrative.Action: Step 0: run `pan sync-main`. If src/lib/computer-use/platform.ts is still absent (PAN-5461 not merged), call task_block on this item with reason "waits for PAN-5461 (provider seam)" and stop; never create or redefine any part of the seam. After the seam lands, do the PRD's seam checkpoint (compare platform.ts exports with PAN-5461 PRD WI-1; follow the merged code where it differs). PRD WI-1 (bridge part), D-2..D-7, D-15, D-16. Extract `parseHelperOutput(stdout, stderr)` from src/lib/computer-use/helper.ts exactly as the PRD's before/after snippet shows (helper.test.ts must pass unchanged). Add `windowsHelperSource()` and `windowsHelperDirCachePath()` to paths.ts. Create src/lib/computer-use/wsl-bridge.ts exporting resolvePowershell, resolveHelperDir (disk cache in ~/.overdeck/computer-use/windows-helper-dir.txt, re-resolve when the cached dir is gone), ensureHelperCopied (sha256 compare, overwrite on mismatch), interopEnabled (binfmt_misc WSLInterop or WSLInterop-late exists), runWindowsHelper (steps and failure mapping exactly as in the PRD; execFile options { env, timeout: 30_000, killSignal: 'SIGKILL', maxBuffer: 64 MiB }; `ok:false` throws helper_error with the helper's message; op file removed in finally; execution-policy stderr regex → the D-4 message). Use promisified execFile only (no sync child process). Every dependency is injectable via WslBridgeDeps; tests use fakes and vi.useFakeTimers() for any timing. Also apply D-17 (set WSL_INTEROP from /run/WSL/*_interop when the env lacks it) and D-18 (copy via runtime.ps1.tmp-<uuid> then rename). Export windowsVersion(deps): one `powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command` call printing $PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString() and [Environment]::OSVersion.Version.ToString() on two lines (10 s timeout), returning { powershell, build }.
